description: Rebuilt from the Identity Wing's rw_mass_write_burst threshold, which counted USN rows of ONE file identity and so could not see a burst across many files. Here: at least 100 files changed or renamed within 5 minutes - UBA's file_edited and file_renamed events, each counting its files (aggregate_count). A burst lasting longer than 5 minutes is counted at its average rate, and the hit says so. A second rule, rw_renamed_to_encrypted_extension, fires on 10 or more files renamed into an archive or encrypted-looking extension (.zip .7z .enc .locked .crypt ...) within 10 minutes. Only the user's document folders count (Desktop, Documents, Downloads, Pictures, Videos, Music, OneDrive), as UBA labels each burst's folder: application caches, Program Files, ProgramData and Windows churn constantly and are left out.
proves: Files were changed or renamed in bulk within minutes, consistent with encryption
author: Crow-Eye Team

steps.label: Files changed or renamed in bulk

conditions.value: ^(?:the Desktop|the Documents folder|the Downloads folder|the Pictures folder|the Videos folder|the Music folder|the OneDrive folder)$

semantic_rules.name: Renamed Into Encrypted-Looking Extensions (Threshold)
semantic_rules.description: 10 or more file renames whose final name has an archive or encrypted-looking extension within 10 minutes (UBA file_renamed events that keep each file's rename chain).

conditions.value: ^(?:the Desktop|the Documents folder|the Downloads folder|the Pictures folder|the Videos folder|the Music folder|the OneDrive folder)$
